# Customization Guide

Source: https://github.com/xylex-group/athena-auth-ui/blob/main/docs/customization.mdx

<!-- Generated manually; kept alongside generated API docs. -->

# Customization Guide

This package now exposes two layers of customization:

1. `AuthProvider` config from `@xylex-group/athena-auth-ui/react` for auth behavior that already belongs to the upstream auth runtime.
2. The HeroUI package `ui` overrides for package-owned copy, routes, class-name slots, loading indicators, and email template metadata.

## Use The AuthProvider For Runtime Behavior

These controls already exist on `AuthProvider` and remain the source of truth for auth runtime behavior:

- `localization`
  Use this for broad text changes across auth and settings screens.
- `redirectTo`
  Use this for the default post-auth redirect target.
- `viewPaths`
  Use this when you want the built-in route segments to change.
- `socialProviders`
  Use this to control which OAuth providers are configured and in what default order.
- `plugins`
  Use this to add or remove package-owned auth features like passkeys, API keys, workspace tooling, theme controls, and organization support.

## Use `ui` For Package Overrides

Pass `ui` either on `AuthProvider` for global defaults or on individual exported components for a local override:

```tsx
import {
  AuthProvider,
  SignInPage,
  type AthenaAuthUiOptions,
} from "@xylex-group/athena-auth-ui"

const ui: AthenaAuthUiOptions = {
  pages: {
    auth: {
      container: "min-h-screen bg-[radial-gradient(circle_at_top,#dbeafe,white_55%)]",
      auth: "shadow-2xl",
    },
  },
  auth: {
    logo: <img src="/brand/logo.svg" alt="Acme" className="h-10" />,
    routes: {
      afterSignIn: "/dashboard",
      signUp: "/join",
      forgotPassword: "/recover-account",
      settings: "/account",
    },
    copy: {
      global: {
        separator: "or keep going with",
      },
      signIn: {
        title: "Welcome back",
        submitLabel: "Enter workspace",
        forgotPasswordLink: {
          label: "Need help signing in?",
        },
        signUpLink: {
          description: "Need an account?",
          label: "Create one",
        },
      },
      providerButtons: {
        labels: {
          github: "Continue with GitHub Enterprise",
        },
      },
      passkeyButton: {
        label: "Use security key",
      },
    },
    classNames: {
      authCardHeader: {
        title: "tracking-tight text-2xl",
      },
      signIn: {
        card: "border border-sky-100",
        submitButton: "bg-sky-600 text-white",
        secondaryLink: "text-sky-700",
      },
      providerButtons: {
        base: "gap-2.5",
      },
      providerButton: {
        base: "rounded-full",
      },
    },
    components: {
      loadingIndicator: ({ kind }) => (
        <span className="inline-flex items-center text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.2em]">
          {kind === "signOut" ? "Leaving" : "Working"}
        </span>
      ),
    },
    methods: {
      passkey: "disabled",
      oauthProviders: {
        google: "hidden",
      },
    },
  },
  settings: {
    sidebar: "hidden",
    views: {
      workspace: {
        label: "Admin",
        order: 0,
      },
      account: {
        order: 1,
        sections: ["userProfile", "plugin:theme", "changeEmail"],
      },
      security: {
        order: 2,
        sections: ["changePassword", "activeSessions", "plugin:passkey"],
      },
      workspaceNotifications: {
        visibility: "hidden",
      },
    },
  },
}

export function AuthRoute() {
  return (
    <AuthProvider authClient={authClient} navigate={({ to }) => router.push(to)} ui={ui}>
      <SignInPage />
    </AuthProvider>
  )
}
```

## What The `ui` Contract Covers

`auth.copy`

- `checkEmail`
- `global.separator`
- `signIn`, `signUp`, `forgotPassword`, `resetPassword`, `magicLink`
- `providerButtons`
- `passkeyButton`
- `resetEmailSent`
- `signOut`

`auth.routes`

- `signIn`
- `signUp`
- `checkEmail`
- `forgotPassword`
- `resetEmailSent`
- `signOut`
- `settings`
- `afterSignIn`
- `afterSignUp`
- `afterForgotPassword`
- `afterResetPassword`
- `afterSignOut`
- `callbackURL`

`auth.classNames`

- `authCardHeader`
- `checkEmail`
- `signIn`
- `signUp`
- `forgotPassword`
- `resetEmailSent`
- `resetPassword`
- `magicLink`
- `signInUsername`
- `providerButtons`
- `providerButton`
- `passkeyButton`
- `signOut`

`auth.components`

- `loadingIndicator`
- `signOutLoading`

`pages`

- `auth`
- `settings`

`settings`

- `navigation`
- `sidebar`
- `views`

`settings.classNames`

- `root`
- `mobileTrigger`
- `mobilePanel`
- `nav`
- `navItem`
- `navItemActive`
- `content`

`settings.views`

- `label`
- `order`
- `sections`
- `visibility`

Use `settings.views` when you want to control which settings pages appear in navigation, how they are ordered, or which built-in sections render inside a page.

Examples:

- `account.sections = ["userProfile", "changeEmail", "plugin:theme"]`
- `security.sections = ["changePassword", "plugin:passkey"]`
- `workspace.sections = ["operations", "security", "documents"]`
- `workspaceNotifications.visibility = "hidden"`
- `organizations.visibility = "hidden"`

## Hide Or Disable Specific OAuth Providers

When you need to remove or soften one provider without changing the rest of the auth flow, use `ui.auth.methods.oauthProviders` directly:

```tsx
const ui: AthenaAuthUiOptions = {
  auth: {
    methods: {
      oauthProviders: {
        apple: "hidden",
        microsoft: "disabled"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- Use `"hidden"` when a provider should disappear entirely.
- Use `"disabled"` when the button should stay visible but non-interactive.
- Use this instead of patching provider buttons with `querySelector(...)` or `MutationObserver`.

The same override also applies when you render `SecuritySettingsPage` or `LinkedAccounts` with a local `ui` prop, so linked-account rows can be hidden or disabled without changing sign-in availability:

```tsx
<SecuritySettingsPage
  ui={{
    auth: {
      methods: {
        oauthProviders: {
          apple: "disabled",
          microsoft: "disabled",
        },
      },
    },
  }}
/>
```

Use that pattern instead of patching linked-account buttons with `querySelector(...)` or `MutationObserver`.

Built-in section IDs:

- `account`: `userProfile`, `changeEmail`
- `security`: `changePassword`, `linkedAccounts`, `activeSessions`
- `workspace`: `operations`, `security`, `communications`, `notifications`, `documents`, `logs`, `sdkLab`
- `workspaceOperations`: `operations`
- `workspaceSecurity`: `security`
- `workspaceCommunications`: `communications`
- `workspaceNotifications`: `notifications`
- `workspaceDocuments`: `documents`
- `workspaceLogs`: `logs`
- `workspaceSdkLab`: `sdkLab`
- `organizations`: `organizationManager`

Plugin-contributed account and security cards use `plugin:<pluginId>` when a plugin contributes one card, or `plugin:<pluginId>:<n>` when it contributes multiple cards.

### Configure Workspace Email Providers And Flows

The workspace communications and logs surfaces use the same provider and flow option arrays for the email composer, email failure creation form, and provider filters. Pass custom options through `workspacePlugin(...)`, the `createAthenaAuthPlugins` bundle helper, or directly to the standalone workspace components.

```tsx
import {
  workspacePlugin,
  type EmailSelectOption,
} from "@xylex-group/athena-auth-ui/plugins"

const providers = [
  {
    id: "smtp",
    label: "SMTP server",
    description: "Send through the workspace SMTP server.",
  },
  {
    id: "postmark-eu",
    label: "Postmark EU",
    description: "Send through the EU transactional stream.",
  },
] satisfies EmailSelectOption[]

const flows = [
  {
    id: "password-reset",
    label: "Password Reset",
    description: "Account recovery emails.",
  },
  {
    id: "billing-receipt",
    label: "Billing Receipt",
    description: "Workspace billing and invoice emails.",
  },
] satisfies EmailSelectOption[]

workspacePlugin({
  emailProviderOptions: providers,
  emailFlowOptions: flows,
})
```

The same shape works with the bundled plugin helper:

```tsx
createAthenaAuthPlugins({
  workspace: {
    emailProviderOptions: providers,
    emailFlowOptions: flows,
  },
})
```

## Settings Composition Patterns

Use `SettingsPage` when the package should stay authoritative for a whole route and your app-specific content can live above or below it.

Use `OrganizationManager` with `SettingsSectionsStack` when you want one mixed stack where package-owned and app-local sections share the same ordering rules.

### Keep local sections adjacent to package-owned organization settings

This is the simplest migration path when the package should own organization management and your app still needs local cards like notification preferences:

```tsx
import { SettingsPage } from "@xylex-group/athena-auth-ui"

export function SettingsRoute() {
  return (
    <div className="mx-auto flex w-full max-w-7xl flex-col gap-4 px-5 pt-4 pb-10">
      <SettingsPage
        view="organizations"
        containerClassName="max-w-none p-0 md:p-0"
      />

      <NotificationPreferencesCard />
      <RecentNotificationsCard />
    </div>
  )
}
```

If `/settings` should resolve directly to the package-owned organizations view, point the organizations path at the settings root instead of keeping a local tabs wrapper:

```tsx
<AuthProvider
  authClient={authClient}
  viewPaths={{
    settings: {
      organizations: "",
    },
  }}
>
  {children}
</AuthProvider>
```

### Mix `SettingsSectionsStack` with app-local sections

Use `SettingsSectionsStack` when you want package-owned sections and app-local sections to participate in the same ordered stack:

```tsx
import {
  OrganizationManager,
  SettingsSectionsStack,
  type AthenaAuthUiOptions,
} from "@xylex-group/athena-auth-ui"

const ui: AthenaAuthUiOptions = {
  settings: {
    views: {
      organizations: {
        sections: [
          "organizationManager",
          "notificationPreferences",
          "recentNotifications",
        ],
      },
    },
  },
}

export function OrganizationSettingsRoute() {
  return (
    <SettingsSectionsStack
      view="organizations"
      sections={[
        {
          id: "organizationManager",
          render: () => <OrganizationManager />,
        },
        {
          id: "notificationPreferences",
          render: () => <NotificationPreferencesCard />,
        },
        {
          id: "recentNotifications",
          render: () => <RecentNotificationsCard />,
        },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

Important detail:

- If `ui.settings.views.organizations.sections` is present, every section you want rendered must appear in that ordered ID list, including app-local IDs like `notificationPreferences`.
- If you omit `ui.settings.views.organizations.sections`, `SettingsSectionsStack` falls back to the order of the `sections` prop you passed directly.

### Keep `OrganizationManager` but own the surrounding frame

When you only need the package-owned organization surface inside a local card or page shell, mount `OrganizationManager` directly and keep the rest of the layout local:

```tsx
import { OrganizationManager } from "@xylex-group/athena-auth-ui"

export function OrganizationSettingsCard() {
  return (
    <div className="space-y-4">
      <section className="rounded-2xl border p-4">
        <OrganizationManager />
      </section>

      <section className="rounded-2xl border p-4">
        <NotificationPreferencesCard />
      </section>
    </div>
  )
}
```

Use this when package-owned member, invitation, and organization-switching behavior is the goal, but your product still wants its own page framing.

## Replace Local Check-Email Routes

Use the route-ready page shells when your app only needs the package flow and not a custom wrapper:

```tsx
import {
  CheckEmailPage,
  ResetEmailSentPage,
  SignInPage,
  SignUpPage,
} from "@xylex-group/athena-auth-ui"

type AuthView =
  | "sign-in"
  | "sign-up"
  | "check-email"
  | "reset-email-sent"

export function AuthRoute({ view }: { view: AuthView }) {
  if (view === "check-email") {
    return <CheckEmailPage />
  }

  if (view === "reset-email-sent") {
    return <ResetEmailSentPage />
  }

  if (view === "sign-up") {
    return <SignUpPage />
  }

  return <SignInPage />
}
```

Pair that with the normal auth route configuration instead of a local status-page implementation:

```tsx
<AuthProvider
  authClient={authClient}
  ui={{
    auth: {
      routes: {
        afterForgotPassword: "/auth/reset-email-sent",
      },
    },
  }}
  viewPaths={{
    auth: {
      checkEmail: "check-email",
      resetEmailSent: "reset-email-sent",
    },
  }}
>
  {children}
</AuthProvider>
```

Use this pattern when your custom route only exists to frame the status view. If the product copy or layout needs to differ, keep the route but delegate the actual content to `CheckEmailPage` or `ResetEmailSentPage` and override copy through `ui.auth.copy`.

Use `hideNav` on `Settings`, `SettingsPage`, `AccountSettingsPage`, or `SecuritySettingsPage` when you want to hide the settings navigation for one instance only.

Use `ui.settings.sidebar = "hidden"` when you want to hide the desktop settings sidebar globally for everything below an `AuthProvider`.

`ui.settings.navigation = "hidden"` remains supported as the existing alias for the same behavior.

`userButton.classNames`

- `unauthenticatedRoot`
- `unauthenticatedLink`
- `trigger`
- `iconTrigger`
- `popover`
- `menuHeader`
- `menuItem`

## Per-Component Overrides

Any component that exposes a `ui` prop merges its local `ui` object on top of the nearest provider value:

```tsx
<SignIn
  ui={{
    auth: {
      copy: {
        signIn: {
          submitLabel: "Open app",
        },
      },
      classNames: {
        signIn: {
          submitButton: "bg-emerald-600 text-white",
        },
      },
    },
  }}
/>
```

The merge order is:

1. Upstream auth runtime defaults
2. `AuthProvider` `ui`
3. Component-level `ui`

Nested link objects also merge by field, so a component-level `signUpLink.label` override does not wipe an inherited `signUpLink.href` or `signUpLink.description`.

## Email Template Keys

The email entrypoint now binds each email component to a stable `templateKey`, an Athena Auth `eventType`, and an `overrideSelector` that tells you which column Athena Auth actually uses when selecting an `email_templates` override.

```tsx
import {
  EmailVerificationEmail,
  getAthenaAuthEmailTemplateCatalog,
} from "@xylex-group/athena-auth-ui/email"

EmailVerificationEmail.templateKey
// "verification_email"

getAthenaAuthEmailTemplateCatalog()
```

### Canonical Athena Auth Keys

These keys line up with the built-in Athena Auth template catalog, so Athena Auth resolves overrides by `template_key`:

| Component | templateKey | eventType | overrideSelector |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `EmailVerificationEmail` | `verification_email` | `user.email.verify` | `templateKey` |
| `ResetPasswordEmail` | `password_reset_email` | `user.password.reset` | `templateKey` |
| `OtpEmail` | `two_factor_otp_email` | `user.sign-in.otp` | `templateKey` |
| `OrganizationInvitationEmail` | `organization_invitation_email` | `organization.member.invite` | `templateKey` |

### Package-Owned Stable Keys

These components also have unique stable package keys, but Athena Auth does not seed a canonical runtime `template_key` for these flows. Create or query overrides by `event_type` instead:

| Component | templateKey | eventType | overrideSelector |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MagicLinkEmail` | `magic_link_email` | `user.sign-in.email` | `eventType` |
| `EmailChangedEmail` | `email_changed_email` | `user.email.changed` | `eventType` |
| `PasswordChangedEmail` | `password_changed_email` | `user.password.changed` | `eventType` |
| `NewDeviceEmail` | `new_device_email` | `user.security.alert` | `eventType` |

## Recommended Override Pattern

Use `localization` when you want broad product copy changes across the auth runtime.

Use `viewPaths` and `redirectTo` when the route structure itself is changing.

## Direct Upstream Auth Routing

For the full request, redirect, header, and cookie ownership model, see
[Auth Proxy, Redirects, And Cookies](./auth-proxy-routing-and-cookies.mdx).

Use the Athena base-url helper when the host app needs to talk directly to a dedicated Athena Auth origin instead of proxying through the current app origin.

When `appendAuthPath` is `false`, a relative auth path now resolves against the configured Athena Auth upstream first. That keeps direct-upstream auth routing stable even when the browser is currently hosted on a different UI domain.

```tsx
import { resolveAthenaAuthClientBaseUrl } from "@xylex-group/athena-auth-ui/athena/base-url"

const directAuthBaseUrl = resolveAthenaAuthClientBaseUrl(
  "/direct-auth",
  "https://auth.athena-auth.com/api/auth",
  { appendAuthPath: false }
)

// https://auth.athena-auth.com/direct-auth
```

Use that pattern for auth route debug flows or any deployment where `ui.<domain>` and `auth.<domain>` are intentionally separate origins.

For the reset-password flow, Athena Auth's working email link format is:

```text
https://<DOMAIN_FRONTEND>/api/auth/reset-password/reset_<PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN>?callbackURL=https://<DOMAIN_FRONTEND>/auth/reset-password
```

That means the `forgetPassword` / `requestPasswordReset` `redirectTo` value should normally be the frontend reset view:

```ts
redirectTo: "https://<DOMAIN_FRONTEND>/auth/reset-password"
```

If you override the reset-password route, keep the emailed `callbackURL` target aligned with that same frontend path.

Use `ui.copy`, `ui.routes`, and `ui.classNames` when the change is specific to this HeroUI package surface.

For canonical emails, create and look up Athena Auth `email_templates` rows by `template_key`.

For package-owned non-canonical emails, create and look up Athena Auth `email_templates` rows by `event_type`, and treat the component `templateKey` as a package-level identifier that helps you map the row back to the matching React email component.

```ts
const verification = getAthenaAuthEmailTemplate("verification_email")
// create row with template_key = verification.templateKey

const magicLink = getAthenaAuthEmailTemplate("magic_link_email")
// create row with event_type = magicLink.eventType
// optionally also persist template_key = magicLink.templateKey for your own cataloging
```

The workspace `EmailTemplatesCard` now edits structured `variableBindings` rows directly.
Each binding captures:

- `name`: the template token name used in the body such as `{userName}`
- `source`: the server-side source address such as `athena.users.name` or `athena.organizations.id`
- `required`: whether Athena Auth should fail closed when that source cannot be resolved

Legacy `variables: string[]` rows still load in the UI and remain editable as a compatibility field, but new Athena Auth setups should prefer `variableBindings`.

If you are building admin email-template payloads outside this UI package, the Athena Auth backend now accepts additive `variableBindings` alongside legacy `variables`. If your local `@xylex-group/athena` types have not picked that field up yet, treat that as an SDK typing gap rather than a backend limitation.

- [WorkspaceLogsSettings](../components/workspace-logs-settings.mdx): Standalone settings-tab wrapper for the workspace logs section.
- [WorkspaceNotificationsPanel](../components/workspace-notifications-panel.mdx): Groups workspace preferences, recent notifications, and inbox items for the notifications section.
- [WorkspaceNotificationsSettings](../components/workspace-notifications-settings.mdx): Standalone settings-tab wrapper for the workspace notifications section.
- [WorkspaceOperationsPanel](../components/workspace-operations-panel.mdx): Groups organization and tenant administration tools for the workspace operations section.
- [WorkspaceOperationsSettings](../components/workspace-operations-settings.mdx): Standalone settings-tab wrapper for the workspace operations section.
- [WorkspacePagination](../components/workspace-pagination.mdx): Public HeroUI component for workspace pagination.
- [workspacePlugin](../functions/workspace-plugin.mdx): HeroUI plugin wrapper that registers the workspace settings tabs, localized labels, and custom workspace view paths.
- [WorkspaceSdkLabPanel](../components/workspace-sdk-lab-panel.mdx): Groups the Athena SDK experimentation surface for the workspace SDK lab section.
- [WorkspaceSdkLabSettings](../components/workspace-sdk-lab-settings.mdx): Standalone settings-tab wrapper for the workspace sdk lab section.
- [WorkspaceSectionCard](../components/workspace-section-card.mdx): Shared titled card wrapper used to frame the workspace-specific admin surfaces.
- [WorkspaceSecurityPanel](../components/workspace-security-panel.mdx): Groups session context, passkeys, API keys, admin credentials, OAuth accounts, and active sessions for the security section.
- [WorkspaceSecuritySettings](../components/workspace-security-settings.mdx): Standalone settings-tab wrapper for the workspace security section.
- [WorkspaceSelectField](../components/workspace-select-field.mdx): Public HeroUI component for workspace select field.
- [WorkspaceSettings](../components/workspace-settings.mdx): Aggregates the full workspace experience by stacking every workspace panel in a single settings view.

# Hooks

Source: https://github.com/xylex-group/athena-auth-ui/blob/main/docs/hooks/index.mdx

# Hooks

This index covers the exported React hooks that power the workspace admin surfaces.

## Items

- [useAdminAthenaClients](./use-admin-athena-clients.mdx): Query hook for the list of admin-configured Athena clients available to the workspace tools.
- [useAdminAuditLogs](./use-admin-audit-logs.mdx): Convenience query hook for recent admin audit logs with a default limit of 20 rows.
- [useAdminAuditLogsQuery](./use-admin-audit-logs-query.mdx): Lower-level audit log query hook that accepts a partial Athena list query and normalizes the default limit.
- [useAdminEmailFailures](./use-admin-email-failures.mdx): Convenience query hook for recent email delivery failures with a default limit of 15 rows.
- [useAdminEmailFailuresQuery](./use-admin-email-failures-query.mdx): Lower-level email failure query hook that accepts a partial Athena list query and normalizes the default limit.
- [useAdminEmailTemplates](./use-admin-email-templates.mdx): Convenience query hook for email templates with a default limit of 25 rows.
- [useAdminEmailTemplatesQuery](./use-admin-email-templates-query.mdx): Lower-level email template query hook that accepts a partial Athena list query and normalizes the default limit.
- [useAdminPastEmails](./use-admin-past-emails.mdx): Convenience query hook for recent outbound emails with a default limit of 15 rows.
- [useAdminPastEmailsQuery](./use-admin-past-emails-query.mdx): Lower-level outbound email query hook that accepts a partial Athena list query and normalizes the default limit.
- [useAthenaTableQuery](./use-athena-table-query.mdx): Public React hook for athena table query in the workspace toolset.
- [useAuthUiOptions](./use-auth-ui-options.mdx): Public React hook for auth ui options in the workspace toolset.
- [useCreateAdminApiKey](./use-create-admin-api-key.mdx): Mutation hook that creates an admin API key through the Athena admin method surface.
- [useCreateAdminAthenaClient](./use-create-admin-athena-client.mdx): Mutation hook that creates an Athena client and invalidates the Athena client list.
- [useCreateAdminEmailFailure](./use-create-admin-email-failure.mdx): Mutation hook that creates a new email failure record and invalidates the failure list.
- [useDataTablePagination](./use-data-table-pagination.mdx): Public React hook for data table pagination in the workspace toolset.
- [useDeleteAdminEmailFailure](./use-delete-admin-email-failure.mdx): Mutation hook that deletes an email failure record and invalidates the failure list.
- [useDeleteAdminEmailRecord](./use-delete-admin-email-record.mdx): Mutation hook that deletes admin email records and invalidates the related email queries.
- [useDeleteEmailTemplate](./use-delete-email-template.mdx): Mutation hook that deletes an email template and invalidates the template list.
- [useDeleteWorkspaceDocuments](./use-delete-workspace-documents.mdx): Mutation hook that deletes workspace documents through Athena Auth storage endpoints and refreshes the document list.
- [useFetchOAuthTokens](./use-fetch-oauth-tokens.mdx): Mutation hook that fetches or refreshes OAuth provider token bundles from the auth client.
- [useResolvedAuthUiOptions](./use-resolved-auth-ui-options.mdx): Public React hook for resolved auth ui options in the workspace toolset.
- [useSendEmailTemplate](./use-send-email-template.mdx): Public React hook for send email template in the workspace toolset.
- [useUpdateAdminEmailFailure](./use-update-admin-email-failure.mdx): Mutation hook that updates existing email failure records and invalidates the failure list.
- [useUploadWorkspaceDocuments](./use-upload-workspace-documents.mdx): Mutation hook that uploads workspace documents through Athena Auth storage endpoints and refreshes the document list.
- [useUpsertAdminEmailRecord](./use-upsert-admin-email-record.mdx): Mutation hook that creates or updates admin email records and invalidates the related email queries.
- [useUpsertEmailTemplate](./use-upsert-email-template.mdx): Mutation hook that creates or updates email templates and invalidates the template list.
- [useWorkspaceDocumentsQuery](./use-workspace-documents-query.mdx): Query hook for workspace documents returned by Athena Auth storage document endpoints.
- [useWorkspaceInboxQuery](./use-workspace-inbox-query.mdx): Query hook for real workspace inbox messages returned by Athena Auth inbox or mailbox endpoints.
- [useWorkspaceNotificationsQuery](./use-workspace-notifications-query.mdx): Query hook for real workspace notification events returned by Athena Auth notification endpoints.
- [useWorkspaceRuntime](./use-workspace-runtime.mdx): Stateful runtime hook that hydrates workspace preferences and activity from session data plus local storage.
- [useWorkspaceSession](./use-workspace-session.mdx): Thin session hook with a 60 second stale window for the workspace experience.

# Athena Auth UI Docs

Source: https://github.com/xylex-group/athena-auth-ui/blob/main/docs/index.mdx

# Athena Auth UI Docs

This folder documents the locally owned public API exported from `packages/heroui/src`.

## Browse

- [Components](./components/index.mdx): 102 public UI components and page shells.
- [Hooks](./hooks/index.mdx): 31 exported React hooks for workspace and admin flows.
- [Functions](./functions/index.mdx): 15 plugin helpers and runtime utilities.
- [Entrypoints](./entrypoints/index.mdx): package export map and root import guidance.
- [Customization Guide](./customization.mdx): provider config, `ui` overrides, loading state slots, route/copy overrides, and email template key mapping.
- [Auth Proxy, Redirects, And Cookies](./auth-proxy-routing-and-cookies.mdx): how `/api/auth`, direct-upstream mode, redirects, Authorization headers, and auth cookies interact.
- [Admin Access](./admin-access.mdx): how Athena Auth admin authorization works and how to fix workspace permission errors.

# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

| Version | Channel | Supported |
| ------- | ------- | --------- |
| 1.11.0 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 1.10.2 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 1.9.2 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 1.9.0 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 1.8.4 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 1.8.2 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 1.8.0 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 1.7.0 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 1.6.0 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 1.5.0 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 1.4.0 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 0.3.0 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 0.2.0 | stable | :white_check_mark: |
| 0.1.0 | stable | :white_check_mark: |

## Reporting a Vulnerability

Report vulnerabilities privately to the maintainers. Include reproduction steps, impact, and affected versions. You will receive an acknowledgement and triage update as soon as possible.
